newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger says National, NZ First good mix.
newsitem.headline: Bolger says National, NZ First good mix.

text.p: Caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Monday his conservative National Party would form a "very comfortable mix" with nationalist New Zealand First.
NZ First says it hopes to choose a coalition partner on Tuesday between National and centre-left Labour, nearly two months after an inconclusive general election.

"I think we would form a very comfortable mix, a very comfortable fit. Obviously there has been a lot of give and take in the negotiations, it's been detailed right across the board...I think we couled make a very, very constructive government," Bolger said in a radio interview.
He denied that National had placed key policies "up for grabs" in the negotiations. "It's not for grabs...It is political parties sitting down and blending two political positions," Bolger said.
He said he was confident his parliamentary caucus, which meets on Monday, would support any reasonable deal with NZ First.
